context_rows.summary: PWR's Q1 2026 revenue of $7.87B is a record high with 20.6% YoY growth, and gross margins improved to 14.1% (from 12.6% in Q4 2025). Yet operating margins collapsed to 4.2% from 6.2% QoQ as SG&A/opex ballooned. This is a stark divergence: the top-line and project-level economics are strong, but cost control is deteriorating. If the opex issue is temporary (investments, ramp costs), the stock could re-rate sharply higher. If it's structural (labor costs, project mix), margins may stay compressed.
context_rows.what_changed: Previous quarters showed more stable operating margins. The sequential drop from 6.2% to 4.2% is the largest in the dataset, and it happened despite record revenue — suggesting the cost issue is acute and needs explanation.
context_rows.why_now: Q1 2026 earnings revealed the widest gap yet between improving gross margins and collapsing operating margins, creating uncertainty about earnings quality and sustainability.
